title: A crank-rocker four-bar
statement: A four-bar linkage has the ground link $O_2O_4 = 100\ \text{mm}$, the crank $O_2A = 40\ \text{mm}$, the coupler $AB = 120\ \text{mm}$ and the rocker $O_4B = 80\ \text{mm}$, assembled open. With the crank at $\theta_2 = 60°$ from the ground line, find the angles $\theta_3$ of the coupler and $\theta_4$ of the rocker, the transmission angle $\mu$, the joint $B$ and the coupler point $P$, $60\ \text{mm}$ along $AB$ from $A$ and $30\ \text{mm}$ off it.

artefact.caption: The linkage at $\theta_2 = 60°$: the angles, the transmission angle and the joints

steps.title: The rocker's angle
steps.note: Closing the loop $a\,e^{j\theta_2} + b\,e^{j\theta_3} = d + c\,e^{j\theta_4}$ and eliminating $\theta_3$ gives Freudenstein's equation in $\theta_2$ and $\theta_4$, with the constants $K_1 = \frac{d}{a} = 2.5$, $K_2 = \frac{d}{c} = 1.25$ and $K_3 = \frac{a^2 - b^2 + c^2 + d^2}{2ac} = 0.5625$. At $\theta_2 = 60°$ its root on the open assembly is $\theta_4 = 64.94°$.

steps.title: The joint B and the coupler's angle
steps.note: B lies on the rocker's circle about $O_4$: $B_x = d + c\cos\theta_4 = 133.88\ \text{mm}$ and $B_y = c\sin\theta_4 = 72.47\ \text{mm}$. The crank pin is $A = (a\cos\theta_2,\ a\sin\theta_2) = (20,\ 34.64)\ \text{mm}$, so the coupler turns through $\theta_3 = \tan^{-1}\frac{B_y - A_y}{B_x - A_x} = 18.38°$.

steps.title: The transmission angle
steps.note: The transmission angle is the acute angle between the coupler and the rocker: $\mu = |\theta_3 - \theta_4| = 46.57°$, well clear of the $40°$ rule of thumb below which the rocker is hard to drive.

steps.title: The coupler point
steps.note: $P$ sits $60\ \text{mm}$ along $AB$ from $A$ and $30\ \text{mm}$ to its left: $P = A + 60\,e^{j\theta_3} + 30\,j\,e^{j\theta_3}$, so $P_x = 20 + 60\cos\theta_3$ less $30\sin\theta_3$ is $67.48\ \text{mm}$, and $P_y = 34.64 + 60\sin\theta_3$ plus $30\cos\theta_3$ is $82.03\ \text{mm}$.

stated: the coupler point $P$, $60\ \text{mm}$ along $AB$ and $30\ \text{mm}$ off it
assumed: the $40°$ rule of thumb for the transmission angle
